steps.intent: Our objective is to secure uninterrupted, principled humanitarian access, including through Bab al-Hawa, while strengthening transparency, cross-line deliveries and protection of civilians, with a gender-sensitive focus. The main difficulty is Russian opposition to a longer mandate and automatic renewal; we therefore propose a six-month extension with a possible further six months subject to a further Council decision, alongside robust reporting on transparency and cross-line progress. We also anticipate sensitivities around accountability language, early recovery and references to civilian casualties, which we have kept factual and generic to secure consensus.

messages.Albania: Albania thanks Ireland and Norway and supports the humanitarian core of the draft. We ask for a full twelve-month renewal of the Bab al-Hawa authorization, or at minimum the removal of the requirement for a further Council resolution, to give humanitarian actors predictable access. We also ask that the text explicitly recall the need for accountability for chemical weapons violations. We stand ready to work constructively.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the humanitarian purpose of the draft and the renewal of cross-border assistance through Bab al-Hawa. We would like the extension to preserve the predictability and Council-agreed language of resolution 2585 (2021), and we ask for safeguards on returns and language ensuring that sanctions do not hamper humanitarian delivery. Brazil remains committed to Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity and will work constructively with the penholder.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the humanitarian mechanism, but the current text does not reflect key concerns. We request the addition of language on lifting unilateral sanctions and on the temporary and exceptional nature of cross-border operations and the transition to cross-line delivery. We also ask to reinforce respect for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity. China will abstain if these concerns are not addressed.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism and thanks Ireland and Norway for their work. We cannot accept a text that conditions the additional six months on a further resolution; the authorization should be for twelve months, or at least automatically extended subject to the Secretary-General’s report. We also call for the inclusion of the Bab al-Salam crossing and for the Secretary-General to assess the need for additional crossing points.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the draft as circulated by Ireland and Norway. The humanitarian situation in Syria is dire, and the renewal of cross-border operations at Bab al-Hawa is urgent to save lives. We welcome the text’s balance on humanitarian access, sovereignty, transparency, and early recovery, and urge the Council to move swiftly toward adoption.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa authorization and thanks Ireland and Norway for their efforts to preserve lifesaving humanitarian access. We would like the text to reinforce that refugee returns must be voluntary, safe, dignified and consistent with international law, and to include a clear operative reaffirmation of the UN-facilitated political process under resolution 2254. We also ask the penholders to ensure the reporting timeline avoids any gap in the authorization.
messages.India: India supports renewal of the Bab al-Hawa authorization and the humanitarian focus of the draft. We ask the penholders to include the established formulation that assistance reach all parts of Syria without discrimination, politicization or preconditions, and to make clear that cross-line and cross-border operations respect Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We would also like OP8 to refer to early recovery and reconstruction needs in that same framework, which would strengthen consensus.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the current text as a balanced and practical compromise that renews the Bab al-Hawa authorization while reinforcing cross-line access, transparency, protection of civilians, and early recovery. We commend the co-penholders for their inclusive and transparent process and encourage the Council to preserve its unity on this life-saving humanitarian file. Kenya will vote in favour and calls on all parties to facilitate full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access through all available modalities.
messages.Mexico: Mexico thanks Ireland and Norway and supports the draft’s focus on humanitarian needs and cross-border access. We ask that the renewal be made as predictable as possible: our preference remains a single twelve-month authorization, and at minimum the second six-month period should not require the adoption of a further resolution. We also ask that references to humanitarian actors be kept general, consistent with our prior explanation of vote.
messages.Norway: Norway strongly supports the draft and thanks Ireland for its leadership; we are pleased to co-sponsor it. We continue to believe the Bab al-Hawa authorization should run for 12 months to ensure predictable humanitarian access, and we ask that OP2 be revised to a single 12-month extension without the requirement for a further resolution. We also request a safeguard in OP9 that monitoring and anti-diversion measures do not impede humanitarian action and remain consistent with humanitarian principles.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support the draft in its current form. Our red line is OP2: the authorization must be for six months only, with no pre-commitment to a further six months; any extension must be considered separately. We also insist on removing unverified casualty figures, politicized accountability language, and references to 'arbitrary detention' that prejudge the Syrian Government, and on adding respect for Syria's sovereignty and the negative impact of unilateral sanctions. We are ready to engage constructively on a streamlined text focused on humanitarian access and transparency.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE appreciates the penholder's efforts but cannot support the current text in its present form. We ask that OP2 provide a predictable 12-month extension until 10 July 2023, without requiring a further resolution, to prevent disruption of lifesaving aid. We also seek stronger language on expanding cross-line deliveries and early recovery, and on preventing diversion to terrorist groups. Without these changes, we would abstain.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports a robust renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mandate and welcomes the penholders’ focus on transparency, cross-line access and protection. The UN has been clear that 12 months is needed to meet humanitarian needs, so we ask that OP2 provide a single twelve-month renewal subject only to the Secretary-General’s substantive report, not a further resolution. We can support the rest of the text on that basis.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the humanitarian purpose of this draft and thanks Ireland and Norway for their work. We ask that OP2 provide a predictable twelve-month authorization and reopen Bab al-Salam, rather than create another six-month political cliff and a further resolution that Russia can use to obstruct aid. The humanitarian needs are too urgent for that cycle, and we can support the remaining text on that basis.

steps.summary: The revised text narrows OP2 to a six-month Bab al-Hawa renewal to avoid a Russian veto while adding safeguards on access, transparency, sanctions, sovereignty and the 2254 political process. It preserves the humanitarian core and should attract broad support, with likely abstentions from China, Russia and the UAE. Expected outcome: 12-0-3.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the draft as a basis and welcomes the added OPCW cooperation. We continue to ask for a twelve-month renewal of the Bab al-Hawa authorization so that humanitarian access is predictable and does not face another cliff-edge in six months. We also seek explicit language on accountability for chemical weapons and other violations. Albania can join consensus on this basis.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the current text. We welcome the incorporation of return safeguards and language ensuring that unilateral sanctions and other coercive measures do not impede humanitarian assistance. The draft preserves the temporary and exceptional nature of the cross-border mechanism and reaffirms Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Brazil encourages the Council to renew the authorization without a gap.
messages.China: China supports the six-month renewal of the Bab al-Hawa authorization and appreciates the inclusion of language on the temporary and exceptional nature of the cross-border mechanism, transition to cross-line deliveries, sovereignty and balanced treatment of unilateral sanctions. However, the reference in OP3 to assessing the need for additional crossing points goes beyond the existing mandate and risks creating pressure for new crossings; it should be replaced by an assessment of cross-line progress and access obstacles. With that change, China can support the draft.
messages.France: France welcomes the partial acceptance in revision 1, in particular the deletion of the further-resolution clause and the added assessment of additional crossings. However, a six-month renewal limited to Bab al-Hawa does not meet the humanitarian imperative or the Secretary-General's repeated warnings; France continues to call for a twelve-month renewal and for Bab al-Salam to be authorized alongside Bab al-Hawa. Predictable, scaled access is essential to avoid another politicized cliff-edge, and we urge the penholder to reflect these points in the text.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the revised draft as a balanced humanitarian compromise. It preserves the Bab al-Hawa authorization while reaffirming Syria's sovereignty, calls for cross-line progress, and includes necessary reporting and transparency. We encourage all members to support it and stress the need for full implementation without politicization.
messages.Ghana: Ghana thanks Ireland and Norway for the revised text and welcomes that our earlier requests on non-refoulement safeguards, reaffirmation of resolution 2254 (2015), and early reporting have been reflected. We can support the draft as it stands, as it preserves humanitarian access through Bab al-Hawa while reaffirming Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and the need for a political settlement. We encourage all members to unite behind the text to avoid a gap in authorization.
messages.India: India supports the revised draft as a balanced basis for renewing the cross-border humanitarian mechanism. Our key concerns—non-politicization, respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and support for early recovery and reconstruction—are reflected in the text. We encourage continued emphasis on cross-line deliveries, transparent and needs-based assistance, and preventing diversion to terrorist groups. India is prepared to support the draft.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the revised draft as a balanced humanitarian text that places the needs of the Syrian people at the centre while respecting Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We welcome the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border operation and the continued emphasis on cross-line deliveries and all available modalities of humanitarian access. Kenya thanks the penholders for their efforts to preserve Council unity and will vote in favour.
messages.Mexico: Mexico appreciates the penholder’s flexibility in deleting the further-resolution clause and in adopting general language on humanitarian actors. Mexico supports the draft but reiterates that a six-month authorization alone is insufficient for predictable humanitarian planning; we therefore ask that OP2 extend the Bab al-Hawa authorization to twelve months, or at minimum provide an automatic additional six months subject to the Secretary-General’s report. Mexico will not block a humanitarian renewal and remains focused on ensuring assistance reaches those in need without politicization.
messages.Norway: Norway supports the current text as the best achievable compromise to prevent a gap in life-saving cross-border assistance. We regret that a 12-month extension could not be agreed, but we welcome the OP10 safeguard on diversion and transparency and the reporting deadline in OP3. We urge all members to adopt the draft without delay.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation welcomes the six-month, Bab al-Hawa-only renewal and the removal of the casualty figure. However, we cannot accept language that opens the door to additional crossing points; that is a red line. We also insist on coordination with the Syrian Government and on preserving national law in detention language, and we oppose politicized references to the OPCW. With these changes, we can support the text.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE appreciates the incorporation of cross-line, early recovery and counter-diversion language. However, a six-month horizon perpetuates uncertainty and risks disrupting lifesaving humanitarian operations. Our red line remains a single twelve-month renewal of the Bab al-Hawa crossing until 10 July 2023, with the reporting timeline adjusted accordingly. If OP2 is amended, we can support the text; otherwise we would abstain.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: We appreciate the penholders’ efforts and welcome the removal of the further-resolution clause. However, the UN has been clear that a six-month renewal is insufficient to meet humanitarian needs, and the UK continues to press for a single twelve-month renewal. Please amend OP2 to extend until 10 July 2023 and adjust OP3’s reporting dates accordingly; we remain ready to support a consensus text on that basis.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the humanitarian purpose of this draft, but the current OP2 falls short of what is needed: a six-month authorization limited to Bab al-Hawa creates another avoidable cliff and leaves a critical crossing unused. We urge the penholders to restore a twelve-month authorization and add Bab al-Salam, and to require an early Secretary-General assessment on additional crossings by 10 September so the Council can act in time. We also ask that OP8 be narrowed to early recovery, with any reconstruction tied to a credible political process under resolution 2254 (2015).

steps.summary: The revision preserves a Bab al-Hawa-only renewal, adding a further six months subject to the Secretary-General's substantive report and thereby avoiding a new resolution requirement. It removes the additional-crossings assessment, strengthens cross-line and access reporting, adds qualified coordination and OPCW language, and ties reconstruction to a credible political process under resolution 2254 (2015). The draft is expected to be adopted with broad support and no veto.

reasons.Albania: Albania is a pro-humanitarian, pro-Western elected member that strongly supports renewing the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism and accountability language. Although it sought a fixed twelve-month renewal, the compromise creates a twelve-month horizon and warrants a yes vote.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil’s stated position was support, it had no requested changes, and it has consistently backed humanitarian renewals while emphasizing sovereignty and cross-line access. A yes vote is consistent with its record and posture on Syria.
reasons.China: China abstained on the Western-backed 12-month cross-border renewal in July 2022, preferring a shorter extension and stronger emphasis on cross-line delivery and the negative impact of unilateral sanctions. The draft’s additional accountability and human-rights language, combined with the unresolved duration issue, made abstention the most consistent position.
reasons.France: France treats renewal of the cross-border mechanism as a humanitarian imperative and has previously supported lesser compromises while expressing regret. The partial acceptance of its requests warrants a yes vote with a pre-vote explanation, not abstention or veto.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon has consistently supported humanitarian resolutions on Syria and was listed as supporting this draft. The text aligns with Gabon’s priorities by preserving life-saving humanitarian access while reaffirming Syrian sovereignty and requiring transparent reporting.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana was recorded as supporting the draft, and the resolution aligns with Ghana’s consistent support for humanitarian access while balancing sovereignty and transparency concerns. Voting in favour also reflects Ghana’s commitment to multilateral humanitarian action in the Security Council.
reasons.India: India’s established position supports life-saving humanitarian access while insisting on respect for Syria’s sovereignty and the temporary nature of cross-border mechanisms. The draft is consistent with India’s prior votes in favour of extending the Bab al-Hawa authorization and broader humanitarian provisions.
reasons.Ireland: Ireland is a co-penholder and co-sponsor of this humanitarian renewal and has consistently supported safe, unimpeded cross-border and cross-line assistance under resolutions 2165, 2585 and 2254. Voting in favour is fully consistent with Ireland’s humanitarian and international law commitments.
reasons.Kenya: Kenya has consistently supported humanitarian renewals for Syria and voted for resolution 2585, prioritising relief access while affirming sovereignty and Council unity. The draft reflects those priorities, so Kenya votes yes.
reasons.Mexico: Mexico has consistently supported humanitarian cross-border operations in Syria and had asked for a twelve-month extension; the penholder accommodated that request through the six-plus-six-month formula, so Mexico votes in favour.
reasons.Norway: Norway is a co-sponsor and a consistent supporter of renewing the UN cross-border humanitarian mechanism for Syria; voting yes reflects its humanitarian priorities and Council record.
reasons.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation was likely to veto the Ireland/Norway draft on 8 July 2022 because it sought a long extension of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism without sufficient emphasis on Syrian sovereignty and cross-line access, despite partial acceptance of Russian amendments.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: UAE’s red line of a single twelve-month renewal was only partially accommodated, so abstention matches its stated negotiation position and practice of not blocking humanitarian aid. Explaining before the vote signals concern while allowing the resolution to proceed.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK strongly supports renewing the Bab al-Hawa humanitarian mechanism and, despite preferring a full 12-month renewal, would not block this compromise when needs are urgent. Voting in favour is consistent with the UK’s record on UNSCR 2585 and its humanitarian and political objectives on Syria.
reasons.United States of America: The United States would vote yes because maintaining the Bab al-Hawa authorization before it expires is a core humanitarian priority, even though the draft only partially meets U.S. requests on duration and additional crossings. The U.S. would use a pre-vote explanation to support the compromise while registering concerns.

before.Albania: Thank you, President. Albania thanks Ireland and Norway for their efforts to bring the Council to a text that responds to an urgent humanitarian imperative. The situation in Syria remains devastating; the United Nations has documented over 300,000 civilian deaths, and millions of Syrians depend on cross-border assistance for their survival. The renewal of the Bab al-Hawa mechanism is a lifeline that must not be interrupted. We regret that the draft does not provide a fixed twelve-month renewal, but we recognize that it establishes a total twelve-month horizon through the six-month renewal and the additional six-month extension, subject to the Secretary-General’s substantive report. We expect full compliance, sustained progress on cross-line access, transparency, and robust monitoring to prevent diversion, while preserving humanitarian principles. Albania will vote in favour. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, ensure unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria, and ensure accountability for all violations, including the use of chemical weapons. We reaffirm our strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria.
before.Brazil: Brazil will vote in favour of this draft. We do so because the humanitarian needs in Syria remain severe and the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border operation is necessary to prevent further suffering. Brazil reiterates that this mechanism is temporary and exceptional, and that full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity must guide all humanitarian operations. We also stress the need to strengthen cross-line deliveries, remove obstacles to humanitarian access, ensure transparency and accountability, and support early recovery projects in line with humanitarian principles. Brazil remains committed to a credible, inclusive political process under resolution 2254 (2015) as the only sustainable path to ending the crisis.
before.China: China supports humanitarian assistance to the Syrian people and the improvement of the humanitarian situation in Syria. The cross-border mechanism is a temporary and exceptional arrangement and should be gradually transitioned to cross-line delivery, with full respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. The draft before us does not fully reflect the concerns of the Syrian Government and other parties and lacks balance on the issue of unilateral sanctions, which are the main obstacle to improving the humanitarian situation. Therefore, China will abstain on this draft resolution.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this resolution. The cross-border mechanism is an indispensable lifeline for millions of civilians in north-west Syria, and the Council must not allow it to lapse. We regret, however, that the text does not include all the elements we considered essential: a guaranteed twelve-month renewal and the authorization of the Bab al-Salam crossing, as humanitarian actors have recommended. We also recall that this mechanism is established by the Council and does not depend on the consent of the Syrian regime. France will remain fully engaged in supporting full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including cross-line deliveries, and accountability for all violations. We reaffirm our commitment to Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and to the political process under resolution 2254 (2015).
before.Gabon: Gabon thanks Ireland and Norway for their efforts and supports the draft before the Council. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains grave, and the renewal of cross-border assistance through Bab al-Hawa is essential to reach millions of civilians in need. At the same time, we emphasize that this mechanism is temporary and exceptional, must be implemented in full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and should be accompanied by stronger cross-line deliveries and transparent reporting. Gabon will vote in favour.
before.Ghana: Ghana thanks the delegations of Ireland and Norway for their efforts in bringing forward this draft resolution. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains grave, and the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism is essential to preserving a lifeline for millions of civilians in need. Ghana will therefore vote in favour of this draft, while emphasizing that humanitarian access must be full, safe, rapid and unhindered, and must be delivered in accordance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. We also stress the importance of respecting Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and of continued progress on cross-line deliveries, transparency and monitoring. Ultimately, only a credible and inclusive political process under resolution 2254 (2015) can deliver a sustainable solution to the suffering of the Syrian people.
before.India: India will vote in favour of the draft resolution. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains grave, and the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border operation is necessary to ensure life-saving assistance reaches those in need. At the same time, we stress that cross-border assistance is a temporary and exceptional measure and must be complemented by strengthened cross-line deliveries, transparency, and early recovery efforts. All humanitarian operations must fully respect Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and be conducted in accordance with humanitarian principles. We call upon all parties to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, protect civilians, and support the credible political process under resolution 2254 (2015).
before.Ireland:
Mr. President,

Ireland, together with Norway, has worked to present a balanced and humanitarian-focused text at a critically urgent moment. The renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border operation is a lifeline for millions of civilians in northwest Syria, including women, children and vulnerable groups, and the Council cannot allow humanitarian access to lapse on 10 July.

The text before us preserves the humanitarian principles, underscores the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, and makes clear that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and exceptional, with strengthened reporting and due attention to cross-line access as conditions permit. It also rightly demands protection of civilians, respect for international humanitarian and human rights law, accountability, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in humanitarian and peace processes.

Ireland will vote in favour of this resolution and urges all members of the Council to do so. We owe the Syrian people no less.
before.Kenya: Kenya will vote in favour of this draft resolution. Our position remains grounded in the humanitarian imperative: the Syrian people must not be made to bear the consequences of political deadlock. We support the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism as a temporary and exceptional lifeline, alongside strengthened cross-line deliveries, transparency, monitoring and full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We urge all parties to ensure safe, unhindered and principled humanitarian access, and we call on the Council to preserve the unity and compromise that made this renewal possible.
before.Mexico: Mexico will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank Ireland and Norway for their efforts to keep the Council focused on the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people. A predictable twelve-month extension of the Bab al-Hawa crossing, through the agreed six-plus-six-month formula and the Secretary-General’s substantive reporting, is essential to allow humanitarian actors to plan and deliver life-saving assistance. Mexico would have preferred an initial twelve-month renewal in a single period, but we recognize that the text before us provides the necessary continuity. Our priority remains full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all parts of Syria through cross-border and cross-line operations, in accordance with humanitarian principles and with full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We also welcome the text’s attention to early recovery, the protection of civilians, and the need to ensure that sanctions and other measures do not impede humanitarian activities. Mexico calls on all parties to facilitate humanitarian access without politicization or discrimination and will support this resolution.
before.Norway: Norway will vote in favour of this draft resolution. As a co-sponsor, we strongly support the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border operation, which remains a humanitarian lifeline for millions of Syrians in desperate need. The Security Council must not allow this authorization to lapse. At the same time, we stress the need for full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access through all modalities, including cross-line deliveries, and we call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians, and facilitate humanitarian assistance. We urge all Council members to support this resolution.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will vote against this draft resolution. We acknowledge that the co-sponsors partially reflected our concerns by removing the assessment of additional crossing points, adding coordination with the Syrian Government, and qualifying the reference to the OPCW and detention language. However, the text remains unbalanced and does not meet the fundamental requirements we have consistently set out. It seeks to perpetuate the cross-border mechanism, which is temporary and exceptional, for an unjustifiably long period without genuine progress on cross-line deliveries. It fails to ensure that humanitarian assistance is delivered in full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national law, and in coordination with the legitimate Government of Syria. It also retains politicized elements, including on the OPCW and accountability, that have no place in a humanitarian resolution. We cannot support a text that ignores the Syrian Government’s role and seeks to impose conditions on humanitarian assistance. The Russian Federation therefore votes against this draft.
before.United Arab Emirates: Mr. President, the United Arab Emirates thanks Ireland and Norway for their efforts. We have consistently supported the cross-border humanitarian mechanism as a lifeline for millions of Syrians. We called for a single, predictable twelve-month renewal so that aid is not repeatedly subjected to political conditions. While we note that this draft foresees a possible extension to 10 July 2023, that extension remains conditional and does not meet the requirement of predictability. The UAE will therefore abstain. We urge all parties to ensure full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access and to advance a political solution under resolution 2254 (2015).
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. The humanitarian situation in Syria is desperate, and the Bab al-Hawa crossing remains a lifeline for millions of people. We would have preferred a straightforward twelve-month renewal, as the United Nations and humanitarian actors have called for, and we regret that the Council has again had to settle for a shorter, conditional extension. But given the urgency of the needs, we support this resolution. We call on all parties to ensure full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including cross-line access, and we expect the Secretary-General’s reports to provide the transparency and detail the Council requires. The United Kingdom remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and to a political settlement under resolution 2254.
before.United States of America: The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. We thank the co-penholders for their efforts to preserve the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism, which remains a lifeline for millions of Syrians. We would have preferred a full twelve-month renewal and the authorization of additional crossing points, including Bab al-Salam, and we will continue to press for expanded and predictable humanitarian access. But allowing this mechanism to lapse would cause grave and immediate harm to civilians. We call on all Council members to support the resolution and on all parties, especially the Syrian regime, to facilitate safe, unhindered humanitarian access, including cross-line deliveries, and to ensure that assistance reaches those in need without diversion.

after.Albania:
Mr. President,

Albania voted in favour of this resolution and deeply regrets that it has not been adopted. Twelve members of the Council supported a renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism because it remains a lifeline for millions of Syrian civilians. The use of the veto in the face of such humanitarian need is profoundly regrettable. It does not diminish the needs of the Syrian people, nor does it relieve the Council of its responsibility.

We thank Ireland and Norway for their efforts to bring the Council together around a humanitarian text. We call on all parties to ensure full, safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access to all parts of Syria, through both cross-border and cross-line routes and in accordance with humanitarian principles. We also call for respect for international humanitarian law, strengthened transparency and monitoring, progress on early recovery, and a credible political process under resolution 2254 (2015).

Albania remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, and we will continue to support every effort to save lives and alleviate the suffering of the Syrian people.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China has explained its position before the vote. We abstained on the draft resolution. China supports humanitarian assistance to the Syrian people and attaches great importance to improving the humanitarian situation in Syria. At the same time, all humanitarian operations must fully respect Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and must be conducted in accordance with the humanitarian principles and the guiding principles of General Assembly resolution 46/182.

The cross-border mechanism is a temporary and exceptional arrangement and should be gradually transitioned to cross-line delivery. We regret that the draft did not fully reflect the concerns of the Syrian Government and other parties and lacked balance on the issue of unilateral sanctions, which are the main obstacle to improving the humanitarian situation. China regrets that the Council could not reach consensus on this important humanitarian issue. We hope all parties will continue consultations, avoid politicizing humanitarian assistance, and work for a balanced outcome acceptable to all. China will continue to support humanitarian assistance to the Syrian people and a political settlement under resolution 2254 (2015).
after.France:
Thank you, Mr. President.

France voted in favour of this resolution and deeply regrets that it was not adopted because of the veto of the Russian Federation. The text before the Council was a reasonable and balanced compromise: it renewed the Bab al-Hawa cross-border operation for a total of twelve months through the six-plus-six-month formula, strengthened reporting and transparency, and preserved respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. It responded to an urgent humanitarian imperative.

A veto in these circumstances is unjustifiable. The cross-border mechanism is an indispensable lifeline for millions of civilians in north-west Syria. It is established by the Security Council and does not depend on the consent of the Syrian regime. With the authorization due to expire on 10 July, the Council cannot allow a gap in humanitarian assistance.

France calls on the Russian Federation to reconsider its position and to engage constructively so that this mechanism can be renewed without delay. We will continue to work with the United Nations and all partners to ensure full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access through all modalities, cross-border and cross-line, in accordance with humanitarian principles. France reaffirms its commitment to Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and to accountability for all violations. The Syrian people must not be held hostage to political calculations.
after.Ireland:
Mr. President,

Ireland deeply regrets that the Security Council has been unable to adopt the draft resolution before it. Twelve members voted in favour. A single veto has prevented the Council from renewing a humanitarian lifeline at the very moment it is most needed. For millions of civilians in north-west Syria, this is not a procedural matter. It is a question of whether food, medicine, clean water and shelter will continue to reach them. The Council should not allow a humanitarian mechanism to lapse in this way.

I thank Norway as co-sponsor and all members who engaged in good faith. The text was balanced and practical. It was anchored in humanitarian principles, affirmed Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, strengthened reporting and transparency, and placed appropriate emphasis on cross-line access while recognising the continuing, temporary and exceptional role of the Bab al-Hawa crossing. We regret that it was not adopted. We listened carefully to the concerns raised by the Russian Federation, but disagreement over modalities cannot justify a collective failure that will be borne by the most vulnerable.

Ireland’s position remains clear: there must be full, safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access to all parts of Syria, through all modalities, including cross-border and cross-line operations, in accordance with international humanitarian law and the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. The cross-border mechanism is temporary and exceptional, and we support strengthened cross-line deliveries. But while needs remain at this scale and cross-line access remains insufficient, the Bab al-Hawa crossing is indispensable.

We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian Government, to facilitate humanitarian access, protect civilians, respect international humanitarian law, and ensure that assistance is delivered without politicisation or diversion. We also reiterate our full support for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and for a credible political process under resolution 2254.

The Security Council must not accept that this issue simply lapses. Ireland will continue to work with Council members, humanitarian partners and all relevant parties to find a way to sustain life-saving assistance to the Syrian people. They should not have to pay the price for the Council’s divisions.

Thank you.
after.Kenya:
Mr. President,

Kenya regrets that the Security Council has not been able to adopt the draft resolution before it. We voted in favour because the humanitarian imperative remains clear: millions of Syrians depend on the Bab al-Hawa cross-border operation for their survival, and the Council must not allow a humanitarian gap.

While we respect the positions of members that voted against or abstained, we appeal to all Council members to redouble efforts and find a pragmatic solution before the authorization expires on 10 July. The needs of the Syrian people must not become collateral damage of political deadlock. We call for continued, full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access through all modalities, including cross-border and cross-line deliveries, in accordance with humanitarian principles and with full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. Kenya remains ready to engage constructively to preserve the Council’s unity and the humanitarian lifeline for the Syrian people.
after.Norway:
Mr. President,

Norway deeply regrets that the Security Council has not been able to adopt this resolution. Twelve members voted in favour of a text that would have preserved the Bab al-Hawa cross-border operation, a lifeline for millions of civilians in north-west Syria. The humanitarian needs are immense, and the Council must not allow this lifeline to lapse on 10 July.

Norway will continue to work with all members, in good faith and in a spirit of compromise, to find a solution before the authorization expires. We call on all Council members to act responsibly and in line with the humanitarian imperative. The Syrian people must not be made to pay the price for political deadlock. Humanitarian assistance must reach those in need, in full respect for international humanitarian law and the humanitarian principles.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation has voted against the draft resolution before the Council, and we wish to explain briefly why. Our vote is not directed against the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people, nor against humanitarian assistance as such. Russia has consistently supported the delivery of aid to all Syrians in need, including through cross-line operations, and has worked in good faith to find a balanced arrangement that respects Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.

We could not, however, support a text that sought to perpetuate an exceptional and temporary cross-border mechanism for an unjustifiably long period without genuine safeguards, clear benchmarks and real progress on cross-line deliveries. The co-sponsors ignored the fundamental concerns we have repeatedly raised. In particular, the draft did not properly reflect the need for coordination with the legitimate Government of Syria, did not address the harmful impact of unlawful unilateral coercive measures, and did not establish a credible path toward the gradual reduction of reliance on the cross-border mechanism as conditions permit. The six-plus-six formula does not remedy these defects; it merely postpones the underlying problems and creates new political leverage.

Russia was ready to engage constructively on a realistic extension, including a shorter and reviewable arrangement, had the penholders shown genuine readiness to accommodate the concerns of Council members and the Syrian Government. Instead, we were presented with a text that could not command the Council’s unity and that politicizes the humanitarian file.

We call on our colleagues not to present the Syrian people with a false choice between an unbalanced draft and the interruption of assistance. The Russian Federation remains open to constructive work on a transparent, effective and sovereignty-respecting humanitarian arrangement for Syria. We urge the penholders to return to consultations in a spirit of compromise.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom deeply regrets that the Russian Federation has vetoed this resolution. Russia alone has blocked the renewal of a humanitarian lifeline for millions of Syrians in desperate need. The Bab al-Hawa crossing is not a political bargaining chip; it is a lifeline. At a time when the United Nations has documented more than 300,000 civilian deaths and when food insecurity and displacement remain severe, this veto will cause avoidable suffering.

The United Kingdom voted in favour because the Council’s response should be driven by humanitarian need, not by political conditions. We regret that the text was already a compromise and did not provide the straightforward twelve-month renewal that the United Nations and humanitarian actors have called for. Even so, Russia has chosen to block it. We call on Russia to reconsider and to allow the Council to fulfil its responsibilities.

The humanitarian imperative has not changed. We will continue to work with Council members and humanitarian partners to sustain cross-border assistance and to press all parties to ensure full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including cross-line access. The United Kingdom remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, to the protection of civilians, and to accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law. The Syrian people must not be abandoned.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States voted in favour of this resolution because the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa crossing is a humanitarian lifeline for millions of Syrian civilians. We deeply regret that a single permanent member—the Russian Federation—has vetoed it, thereby blocking a 12-month extension that would have allowed humanitarians to plan and deliver food, medicine, water and shelter to people in desperate need.

There is no humanitarian justification for this veto. Russia has chosen to put politics before the lives of Syrian women, children and men. It has made clear that it will use its seat on this Council to impose conditions and undermine the cross-border mechanism, despite the overwhelming support of Council members and the clear recommendation of the United Nations and humanitarian partners.

The United States will not abandon the Syrian people. We will work urgently with our partners and across the United Nations system to preserve life-saving assistance, including cross-border and cross-line operations, and to hold accountable those who obstruct humanitarian access. We call on all Council members to join us in insisting that aid not become a pawn. The Security Council must not allow the expiry of this mechanism to become another death sentence for civilians. Russia’s veto does not end this Council’s responsibility—it only deepens it. Thank you.
